b: Home language: Large language models trained on real-life speech recorded in babies’ home environments support the theory that such input is sufficient to engender their language acquisition, according to a new study. Investigators recorded 12 hours of sound per day in the homes of eight different families for the first 1,000 days of the children’s lives. Artificial-intelligence models built with these datasets learned to distinguish speech sounds and built vocabularies of thousands of words in ways that mirrored each child’s development. This approach “offers a framework for translating theories of how children learn into computational models that can be tested directly against children’s real-world development,” the authors write.
